subject.title: feat: contextual group activation — LLM-driven peeking/engaged state machine

question: Should OpenClaw add LLM-driven contextual activation for group chats, and should that behavior live in core shared activation or behind a plugin/channel API seam?
rationale: Automation can prove the current gap, but cannot choose the privacy boundary, provider exposure, config contract, channel coverage, or long-term ownership for processing unmentioned group traffic.

options.title: Sponsor a default-off design first
options.body: Approve a maintainer-owned design with explicit consent, provider exposure, retention/logging, config schema, channel coverage, and tests before accepting implementation.

options.title: Narrow to non-LLM attention behavior
options.body: Pursue timer or mention-window ergonomics separately without introducing a model-driven background peeking path yet.

options.title: Defer to plugin/API seam
options.body: Wait for an observation or decision-hook API that can support this as a plugin-owned capability without baking optional policy into core.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a default-off design first
recommendation.body: Approve a maintainer-owned design with explicit consent, provider exposure, retention/logging, config schema, channel coverage, and tests before accepting implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest history across the central activation and mention-policy code paths.
